summary: Unpredictable autoscale starvation in dedicated pool traced to intermittent silent prefetcher
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightNote reports sudden p99 throughput collapse on their dedicated pool during mid-morning traffic windows. Impact: production inference jobs experience elevated p99 (8-12x baseline) and a surge of 429s and backend-attach timeouts, lasting 5-20 minutes in recurring pulses. Environment: prod dedicated pool assigned to BrightNote, region us-west; model pinned to redwood/open-7b-v2; Dedicated plan with reserved GPUs.

Observed behavior / Steps to reproduce: 1) Normal traffic with sustained small-stream bursts from customer connectors. 2) Autoscaler appears to not provision additional slots even when attach-queue grows. 3) GPU attachments succeed eventually but with high queue latency; subsequent worker prefetchers show long blocking times. 4) When the pulse ends, throughput returns to baseline.

Initial evidence / Logs: - Autoscaler logs show "attach_backoff" events correlated with p99 spikes (timestamps: 2026-03-10T09:12Z, 2026-03-10T09:29Z, 2026-03-11T10:03Z). - Serving runtime metrics show healthy free GPU memory but high prefetch/kv-cache wait times and elevated NVME IO wait. - Prefetcher subsystem traces exhibit silent retries: prefetch request enters queue but never emits a cache-warm event for several seconds, effectively holding batch slots open. - Customer-side telemetry indicates many short streams with keepalive enabled, often 200-400ms inter-request gaps.

Customer impact and urgency: BrightNote is experiencing user-facing slowdowns during business hours (~us-west morning). They are on a dedicated contract and expect predictable throughput. We escalated to P1 due to revenue impact and SLA risk.
investigation_notes:
Timeline of investigation: 1) 2026-03-10 10:00 - Support intake from BrightNote (Aisha K). 2) 2026-03-10 10:30 - Collected autoscaler and allocator traces (Diego M). 3) 2026-03-11 - Replayed request patterns in staging and reproduced queue-hold pattern using a short-stream generator. Hypothesis: an intermittent prefetcher path is entering a backpressure state when many small short-lived streams hammer the prefetch queue; the prefetcher holds resources while waiting on NVMe-backed KV reads, preventing the autoscaler from seeing available capacity and causing attach_backoff. Evidence: - Reproduction in staging with synthetic workload produced same p99 spikes when prefetch concurrency set to 64 and NVMe latency injected. - Kernel-level NVMe IO wait spikes align with prefetch hold durations. - Metrics show slot-leak-like behavior: batch slots blocked by prefetch futures even when GPU memory is free.

Intermediate mitigation tried: - Reduced prefetcher concurrency in prod pool for BrightNote (rolled to 0.5x) for 15 minutes: observed partial relief (p99 down by ~30%) but recurring pulses persisted. - Temporarily increased autoscaler aggressiveness (lower attach_backoff threshold): led to more failed attach attempts and transient 5xxs; reverted.

Open questions: - Why do prefetch requests block indefinitely for short periods instead of failing fast? - Are there pathological client connection patterns that amplify prefetch queue coupling? - Is NVMe IO contention coming from background snapshotter or other tenants on the host?
resolution_notes: Workarounds and next steps: - Short-term (within 24h): Keep prefetcher concurrency reduced for BrightNote pools and enable a conservative fast-fail timeout on prefetch futures (feature flag rollout). Monitor for decreased slot-holding. - Medium-term: Implement prefetcher circuit-breaker that fails prefetch if NVMe latency exceeds threshold; add per-tenant prefetch accounting to prevent silent hold. - Long-term: Scheduler change to surface 'slot held by prefetch' as actionable telemetry to autoscaler so it can treat held slots as unavailable and provision more aggressively.\n\nFollow-ups: - Action item assigned to Diego M: implement prefetch fast-fail flag in serving runtime (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5284) and run canary in us-west with BrightNote traffic pattern. Due date: 2026-03-18. - Action item assigned to Storage team: investigate NVMe tail latency and snapshotter schedule on affected hosts (ticket INT-3321).
